about: THE HOARDS - real hoards of the period, where they were found, when buried, what they held (silver in grams), the landmarks round them (placed from open data) and the clue as measures (from a landmark toward another, so many paces of 1.48 m on the map) that land on the find. Made by Bake/guide/make_chest_data.py from Plans/environment_research/m3.

hoards.name: The Cuerdale hoard
hoards.kind: Viking silver: coins and bullion
hoards.held: More than 8,600 pieces: silver coins, ingots, arm-rings and other jewellery, and cut silver, packed in small bags in a lead chest.

Samlesbury

landmarks.then: yes (the river may have shifted a little (?))

hoards.name: The Vale of York hoard (the Harrogate hoard)
hoards.kind: Viking silver in a church cup
hoards.held: 617 silver coins and 65 other pieces: a gilt silver cup (made in the Frankish lands, probably for a church), a gold arm-ring, silver arm-rings, neck-rings, brooch pieces, ingots and cut silver. The coins and silver were packed inside the cup.

landmarks.then: the rock, yes; the castle, no

hoards.name: The Silverdale hoard
hoards.kind: Viking silver in a lead box
hoards.held: 201 silver pieces in and under a lead box: 27 coins, 10 arm-rings, 2 finger-rings, 14 ingots, 6 brooch pieces, a fine wire braid and 141 bits of cut arm-rings and ingots.

landmarks.then: yes (the shore point; it wears and grows (?))

landmarks.name: Beeston Crag (the old hillfort on it)

hoards.name: The Bedale hoard
hoards.kind: Viking ingots, neck-rings and a sword's gold
hoards.held: 48 pieces: 29 silver ingots (40-146 g each, some nicked to test them), 4 silver neck-rings (one cut in two), a silver arm-ring, a silver brooch, and an iron sword pommel with gold foil, 4 gold hoops and 6 gold rivets from a sword hilt.

hoards.name: The Galloway hoard
hoards.kind: Viking treasure in two layers, with a Frankish lidded pot
hoards.held: More than 100 pieces of gold and silver in two layers: silver ingots and arm-rings (5 with runes), a silver cross, Anglo-Saxon and Irish brooches, a silver lidded pot from the east wrapped in silk, a gold ingot, a gold bird-shaped pin, glass beads and rock crystal.

landmarks.then: (?): today's church is 18th c; an older church there is not known for 900

hoards.kind: Viking army silver with the 'Two Emperors' coins

hoards.name: The Dunmore Cave hoards
hoards.kind: Viking silver hidden in a cave
hoards.held: 1999: 43 pieces of silver and bronze in a rock cleft deep in the cave: silver ingots and cone-shaped buttons woven from fine silver wire. 1973: a few Viking-age coins (?).

landmarks.name: the mouth of Dunmore Cave (Dearc Fearna)
Kilkenny: the round tower at St Canice's

measures.then: underground: past so many chambers to the far cleft (the 1999 find lay in a cleft deep in the cave; the chambers are not counted in the open sources (?))

sea_leg.direction: north
sea_leg.route: down the Suir, up the Barrow to New Ross, up the Nore past Inistioge and Thomastown to Kilkenny (how far boats went is (?)), then overland north to the cave

hoards.name: The Skaill hoard

hoards.name: The Hoen hoard

hoards.kind: Rus silver at the Dnieper portage
hoards.held: Silver jewellery of the 10th c. Seven hoards in all are known at Gnezdovo, with more than 1,100 Arabic coins and Byzantine coins, and a Byzantine dish.

landmarks.name: the hill-fort of Gnezdovo (the central settlement, where the Svinets meets the Dnieper)
the Ol'shanka stream at the Dnieper (?)

measures.then: the barrows lie round the fort: the 1867 spot is not known closer

measures.at: among the barrows by the fort (no open positions found for the barrow groups)

sea_leg.direction: the hoard lies at the port

hoards.name: The Westerklief hoard (Wieringen)
hoards.kind: Viking silver in Frisia
hoards.held: Silver coins, ingots and jewellery: 1.7 kg. Smaller hoards of the same time were later found in the same area.

landmarks.name: Oosterklief (the east cliff)
landmarks.then: (?) the boulder-clay cliff is old; the hamlet is not known then

turn.how: turn square to the string (a right angle) and pace on

measures.then: up on the high ground, in the meadow (ours: the meadow is not published)

sea_leg.direction: north-west across the waters to Wieringen
sea_leg.note: (?) The coast of 860 was very different (no Zuiderzee yet): only the straight distance is given.

hoards.name: The Fécamp hoard
hoards.kind: Norman and Frankish deniers in two pots
hoards.held: Several thousand silver deniers and half-deniers in two earthenware pots: at least 3,107 of Richard I (Rouen), 2,478 of Hugh (Rouen), 2,426 or more of Charles the Bald, and others from Auxerre, Cambrai, Chartres, Laon, Le Mans, Limoges, Paris, Quentovic, Verdun and more.

landmarks.name: the dukes' palace
landmarks.then: (?) the dukes lived at Fécamp in the 10th c; the standing remains are later

landmarks.name: the church of the Holy Trinity
landmarks.then: (?) Richard I's church was built in the 980s, consecrated 990

turn.how: turn square to the string (a right angle) and pace on

measures.then: two pots: dig twice

sea_leg.direction: down the Seine to its mouth, then north-east along the chalk cliffs of Caux past Étretat to the Valmont mouth
sea_leg.note: (?) our route; the Seine bends are drawn coarsely.

also.fiscannum: from 990 the hoard lies at the port
